:::{#def-unit-vector}
#### Unit vector

A **unit vector** is a vector whose Euclidean norm (@def-euclidean-norm) is $1$.
A unit vector is said to have *unit length*.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-unit-vector}
#### A unit vector and a vector that is not one

For $\vx = (0.6, 0.8)$:

$$
\ba
\norm{\vx}
&= \sqrt{0.6^2 + 0.8^2}
&& \text{(definition of the norm)}
\\
&= \sqrt{0.36 + 0.64}
&& \text{(square)}
\\
&= \sqrt{1}
&& \text{(add)}
\\
&= 1
&& \text{(take the square root)}
\ea
$$

so $(0.6, 0.8)$ is a unit vector.
The vector $(1, 1)$ is not:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\norm{(1, 1)} &= \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} \\
&= \sqrt{2} \\
&\ne 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
